properties.description: Two test files, written first and observed failing on main (b19b49d): crates/reflow2-core/tests/an_inference_says_how_premises_support_a_conclusion.rs (10 tests, scratch in-memory stores, generic write path) and crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/an_inference_says_how_premises_support_a_conclusion.rs (4 tests over the served MCP surface). They check: AND by default (one failing premise: not delivered, broken); the requirement's SHOWN WHEN literally (redundant support marked any; one support removed: weakened and still standing; the last: broken); k of n at k-1 and k; Kleene unknown; modus ponens (all over P and P → Q, rule_name modus ponens; P fails: Q broken); a claimed met that does not follow raises conclusion_does_not_follow and one that follows raises none; a circle refused at write; a chain that breaks through a broken conclusion and stops at a weakened one; two derivations read as ANY; add_inference refusing a bad rule or k with its legal values and writing nothing; and a design with no Inference reporting byte for byte as main did (fixture recorded on main).
properties.findings: On branch feat/an-inference-says-how-premises-support-a-conclusion at 101d784, in a warm worktree under the shared build lock: core 10/10 and MCP 4/4 pass; the core suite passes whole on the in-memory backend (226 test binaries); a full workspace run (400 binaries) failed only the 5 registries a new tool and type must join, which pass after 101d784. On main b19b49d the same files failed: core 9 of 10 at their first write ("Unknown node type: Inference"; the tenth is the no-Inference guard recorded on main) and MCP 4 of 4 ("no tool named add_inference is served").
properties.name: An Inference's rule is checked in the roll-up, the change walk and the finding; nothing changes without one
